PLEASE READ BEFORE BUYING THIS GAME YOURSELF! There is a jumpscare where Tanner can SA the player. This is not warned anywhere in-game, or on the steam page, and it's not clear how to avoid this jump scare until you've gotten it at least once. I know this series is no stranger to topics like that, but it happening to the player in an animation is a different level than reading about it on a fictional webpage. Edit: And I'd like to make it very clear, my problem IS NOT with the jump scare itself, or Tanner as a character, and I'm not asking for the jump scare to be removed or changed. This aspect of his character was already hinted at in Scrutinized, and like I said this series is no stranger to these things. I posted this review as a warning to anyone potentially sensitive to the topic. The mature content warning already exists at the bottom of the steam page and could have easily mentioned this as well, especially after Tanner was used so much for marketing and hyping up the game. I will change my review if proper warnings are added because otherwise, this is a really fun game and I love the series.

Unlike the previous WTTG, this one seems a little too buggy and counterintuitive to be beatable. Even after downloading the PDF for information on the threats there's no clear indicators on how to prevent the instakills. Tanner seems to have no grace-period early game which makes things incredible inconvenient to play. I haven't found any sound-cues or seen him ahead of his instakill animations. Even looking through the curtains of the motel windows he doesn't appear before his instakills. The game also needs to tweak the sound variations a bit, hack sound cues are BLARINGLY loud to the point where it's far too uncomfortable to play with sound anywhere above 30%. This makes footsteps and such impossible to hear. Sometimes the panic button on the front desk doesn't work, and the computer hacks seem to have no consistency with difficulty- sometimes they randomly become insanely difficult and force you to have a SLED on you at all times. Conclusion (Mostly my opinion): Game needs some serious rebalancing, especially for a "normal" mode. Add sound sliders, especially for the hack sound. Give a little more insight on the 'threats pdf', I shouldn't need to wait a couple weeks for a wiki on this game to understand how to thoroughly prevent Tanner early in a run.

Extremely frustrating in its current state, I have died many times and gotten set back 10+ minutes with no gained information on what I could do differently. Ethernet went out? I died going outside to fix it despite not hearing any noises like the threats guide told me to watch out for. I heard spooky music? The power went out at the same time and I died as I went into the room marked with the Ace despite running as fast as my stamina would let me. Lucas killed me? Sucks to suck, I was too busy getting ear raped by the hacking noise to hear a tiny lockpicking noise. There's no way to turn down the volume of the hacking noise so if Lucas just so happens to come after you, you're dead no matter what because you literally cannot hear him. The game also just does not explain certain things properly. I spent five minutes thinking I was soft-locked because the game fails to tell you that in addition to the main power room, which is how power outages worked in the second game, there is ALSO a breaker on the opposite side of the motel, outside, that has a single switch that can be flipped off or on. The checkpoints help but it's still annoying as ♥♥♥♥ to be set back 10 minutes and having to go back and do the exact same thing you just did while hoping you make it to the next checkpoint without dying Edit: I found out that you're supposed to not move AFTER the animation for fixing the ethernet is done. I had assumed that I was killed because I was stuck in the animation while Tucker was active because I heard footsteps right after starting the animation, so I took that as a sign that I had done something wrong prior to the animation. I think maybe a game over tool tip may have helped, especially while the game is so new and there isn't a crazy amount of information about every encounter yet.

I should preface this by saying I beat every Reflect Studios game in a row without dying (completed the gauntlet challenge). This game is an unbalanced mess, that was released untested. The enemies are really unfair, you can get double enemies scenerios where you just die and no, the patch that was released doesn't work. Game Dev releases patches that actively slow down the players and make the gameplay worse and focuses on paid DLC skins instead of working on improving the gameplay. What are we doing? People have been waiting 8 years for this game and it's NOT good, even content creators are not having fun. The game released in what I feel like is an early access state. The dev stated before release that there will be 5 endings, but on release he said there are only 2 available because the rest wasn't finished. What are we doing? This game has been delayed by 9 MONTHS from its original October 2025 release date and its this unfinished? This game is the weakest Reflect Studios game yet, go buy WTTG2 or Dead Signal instead. I will update this review if the dev decides to fix the issues with the game instead of focusing on monetization. Avoid. EDIT: Dev harassed me after I left this review. Sad to see he's witch hunting people who leave honest reviews.

Edit: The button issue has been nerfed, which is great. The dev is working hard on getting patches out quickly, which is also great. This game has a great chance to rival WTTG 2. However, it should not have launched in this state. I know over time things will get smoothed over, (cherry picking an example here) but even with the latest hotfix, there's now a new "feature" where you get punished just for checking for a threat. I understand it's to prevent just spamming the button, but checking for Tanner once every 10 in game minutes is not in my eyes "spamming" the button yet I had to go fix the internet very quickly after checking a few times. Regardless, using the button repeatedly to check for Tanner in my opinion adds to the flow state these kind of games love to put you in and needs to be reverted, or how using the button degrades your internet needs to be seriously nerfed. Thumbs up just because I know what this game will become as it gets fixed over time but it's a little too brutal in a bad way in this state.

This was my first experience with the Welcome to The Game series, and I haven't had the greatest time so far. This game is currently too unbalanced to be fun- overlapping killers that you have no hope of surviving, sparse ways to make money early-game, unfair killers that are basically just an RNG check to see if you survive or not. This game also has the FNAF 4 effect where having your volume up dictates whether or not you survive. If you play games using a speaker system like me, you will immediately be at a disadvantage- it's very annoying. I sadly can't recommend it in this state... wait until the developer fixes/reworks it and then consider purchasing this game (I will also change my review if he does fix it). Also, the dev recently put out a hotfix that makes your limited toolset to defend yourself even worse... kind of a slap in the face lol.

Do I like the game? Yes... But there are some huge glaring issues that make me almost want to leave a negative review. SOUND CUES in this game ARE absolutely HORRENDOUS, as the game is already really quiet to begin with. I have to crank my headphones to max volume to hear the assassin, tanner, and tucker. Only to get ear blasted because of the hacking sound which is still extremely loud. Audio just needs a whole rebalance in this game especially since the gameplay revolves around it. A player shouldn't be second guessing themselves on ambient noises to know if it's the killer coming, it should be clear and decisive if you're paying attention to them. This alone makes me want to say not to buy it until it gets fixed or reworked, but the web browsing and computer stuff is fun so I'll deal with it.

This game feels unfinished, yet it is being sold at a relatively high price without being clearly labeled as Early Access. Several core gameplay mechanics are either broken or severely bugged. In-game websites and PDF files frequently fail to load. The only workaround I have found is changing the display resolution to 1920×1080, even though my native resolution is 3440×1440. Since the most recent patch, scrolling through in-game websites has also become extremely laggy and unreliable. Another major issue is that the in-game internet connection disconnects every three to five minutes of in-game time. This often prevents any further progress and forces the player to repeatedly run back and forth to restore the connection. While returning, a hacking event will often begin. Even when attempting to defend against the hack, the player can be killed, resulting in the entire process having to be started again from the beginning. In its current state, making meaningful progress is extremely difficult. The experience is frustrating, repetitive, and unnecessarily time-consuming. It almost feels as though the game is designed to consume enough time that players exceed the refund window before realizing how broken it is. This is not acceptable, even for an indie game. EDIT: Refunded. Thanks to Steam Support for handling it. I might check the game again in one or two years, once it is fully functional and available for half the price. However, I am done paying full price for unfinished and broken games while the developers expect paying customers to act as unpaid testers and help them fix the product. That is exactly what Steam’s Early Access program is for. If the game had been released and priced accordingly as Early Access, much of this criticism could have been avoided. Releasing it as a supposedly finished product at full price makes the backlash entirely understandable. At this point, it is difficult not to assume that the decision was motivated primarily by greed.

Between constantly getting hacked, frequent power outages, and waiting for sites to load, only to waste time searching for clues that don't exist, the game also expects you to stay hyper-vigilant at all times. Miss one sound cue, and it's game over. Unfortunately, many of those sound cues are incredibly quiet, while the jump scares are incredibly loud. So you have to choose between dying to threats you could not possibly have heard, or turning the volume up and risking permanent hearing damage from the jump scares. There is an item that makes the sound cues louder, but by the time you can afford it, you are probably already dead. Item prices in general seem way too high considering how important some of the items are. Did I mention that downloading files costs money too? That's right, even after finding a clue in the form of a link, you might have to pay a ridiculous sum to download the corresponding file. You are basically permanently broke because the prices aren't balanced in the slightest. Lastly, every death thus far has felt completely unjustified. The game gives you a short description of the various threats, but some are borderline unavoidable in practice.

Oh and, hacks taking away reputation may sound good in theory, but in actual practice just makes the game feel a lot more tedious then fun. I see the positives though, the gameplay loop is good, but the balancing is a mess. I’m not calling the game a broken nightmare that should have never released, I’m just stating that the balancing needs to be fixed in order for this game to truly release its full potential. I hope you can take this moment to reflect upon the game, and give the well deserved patch it needs.

[h1]This is a very strong contender for the best in the series.[/h1] The music is nice. The location, the motel is a really cool environment to occupy during a run. There's extremely fun interplay with all the mechanics. The new systems for making money are engaging and fun. The rep system, though a bit restrictive early in a run (no longer the case with the new patch), does give the game an interesting sense of progression. And the number of killers makes run variety a guarantee, ensuring something interesting is almost always happening. [b]But what's more important than praise right now is criticism,[/b] as the game is still being updated, with more content planned for the future and I hope it gets even better, so here are some of my thoughts: On the point of the killers, I will say some of them disappointed me slightly in their use. The game is already tough as nails so to ask more is greedy, but seeing a killer like The Breather who was an insanely tough threat in all previous games be reduced to a sprint check is a little disappointing. He went from being the character I feared the most in WTTG2 and Dead Signal to someone who doesn't pose much of a threat. I feel kind of bad for him. Killers like the Noir have gone from simple to incredibly interesting with all the different ways they can spawn and how you need to react to their presence. Having killers be one-note like The Breather makes them feel less like killers out to get you and more like a videogame trigger you half pay attention to. One small thing I wish I knew in my first full run-through was when the cut-off time was. I had no idea the game time limit was 4AM because as far as I know (I swear I looked) it isn't stated anywhere. When it would be a very simple thing to have Ronald simply tell you: "If you don't send me the code by 4AM tonight, or if another player completes the puzzle first, you lose." Simple :) It would also be cool to be able to remove pinged users from your CryptChat, or move them to a separate "read" section of the program. You spend a lot of time interacting with a whole host of other people on the dark web to make money and buy services, but eventually you don't need some of these people anymore, or they don't need you. To be able to get rid of those useless chats so the side-bar is more neat would allow players to more efficiently manage their contacts in the middle of a run where efficiency can mean the difference between winning and losing. Also one small thing. I don't have the game code to check for certainty but I couldn't really tell if hacking another player of the game slowed their progress towards keys. I had a really tight 3AM - 4AM that I had to retry a bunch because of money troubles and I thought about the idea of spamming the leading player with petty hacks to slow them down until I had enough money to put a hit on them. I don't know if this worked but I certainly would expect that it should in a game like this. If that isn't currently a consideration implimented within the game, maybe it should be? I had a lot issues with the hacking minigames unfrotunately. Firstly, because killers can arive while a hack is happening, (something I like btw), this means you can be faced with downright impossible situations. For example, one time I was grabbed by Cletus after a hack had just began and the long animation of him searching me for the drugs caused me to lose a high level memDefragger hack with absolutely nothing I could do about it. No chance to attempt the hack or use a NOPSled like I would if Lucas had arived at that point instead. I lost all my money and decided to just restart from my checkpoint. I also had an instance where the internet being cut off during a hack caused the hack to disappear and boot me to the desktop. But despite that, the hack was still running, it was just impossible to interact with, so I lost all my money there too. The balancing on some of the hacks is also absurd. The same high difficulty hack of one type may take you a few seconds to a minute and be reasonably doable, although still tough, like StackPusher, MemDefragger and ShiftSEQ (ShiftSEQ is very easy though). But then you have K3RN3LC0MP1L3R and TOKENINE which go WAY overboard on expectations to the point of being nigh impossible. In the case of K3RN3LC0MP1L3R, the speed at which you need to read and then type each line is completely unrealistic, you are not given nearly enough time to get it done. And if you were given enough time the max level hack would take you minutes to finish which is time you simply do not have to spare in many tight normal runs, let alone a 1337 mode run. TOKENINE is a bit more doable but the patterns with the right angles and dots don't have enough unique parts to them to correctly identify the 5 parts of the whole. And again, you aren't given nearly enough time to work it out. Maybe it's a skill issue, I always have to ask myself that with an Adam game, but the disparity in difficulty is laughable when compared to StackPusher and especially ShiftSEQ. Overall, the game is incredibly fun and the way it expects more from you than most games do is something I REALLY appreciate. I got done with a normal mode run on the day I'm writing this and am excited to try a Normal+ run. (Normal deathless) and hopefully eventually feel confident enough to try 1337 mode. Banger game Adam :D [i]~ Review made on July 20th 2026[/i]

Best game in the series with the most demanding learning curve (number of mechanics and things to multitask). Devs are dropping daily patches to address numerous bugs at launch which made the game unplayable and impossible, which most of the negative reviews are about. Most of the game-breaking bugs seems to have been fixed already in just 4 days. The difficulty is punishing but also forgiving on normal mode due to the new checkpoint system with every in-game hour. Remember that these games are designed to be overwhelming and extremely difficult when you first start out knowing nothing: Expect to die a lot. There will be lots of trial and error, especially with the less you know about the mechanics. Non-spoiler tips and recommendations for everyone: • If you have any problem with audio in this game (like inaudible audio cues, or too loud hack sound), please apply Loudness Equalisation for your audio device in windows sound settings, it will fix (or at least help) everything without feeling like a cheat. Just remember to enable/disable it whenever you open/close the game, and keep this window open so you can easily do it. • The slots gambling mechanic is not at all necessary to win, getting lucky can help but you'll be fine without ever touching it. • Normal Mode has checkpoints every in-game hour. Make use of these to learn the game. It's very nice that you don't have to reset the entire run when learning, though you may feel a desire to reset runs as a learning opportunity to go for a better strategy! • At the start of your run, install A.C.R.S. I'm not sure why this isn't part of the tutorial! • Make plenty of use of the steam overlay's built in note taking feature. I like all the new models and the voice acting. The new animations especially are a big improvement. I don't like how obnoxiously loud the hack sound is. The Windows audio loudness equalization tip I talked about above slightly helped with this, because it meant I could play the game at a little bit lower volume overall, but still... it's really loud.

[h1] Easily the best game in the series [/h1] I went into this game completely blind, and it's been really fun, immersive and scary. I’ve had a great time streaming it to my friends on screenshare. I'm also an absolute coward when it comes to horror games, so this is helping me get over that, even though I screamed so loud at a Tanner jumpscare that my family thought I died lmao. The only time I genuinely got stuck and had to look up an outside guide was to figure out where the bomb was. [b] If you [/b] enjoyed watching playthroughs of Welcome to the Game I & II or FNAF, you should definitely buy this. Playing it yourself is a whole different level; The closest thing I can compare it to is that it feels like FNAF on steroids, Noir are basically Golden Freddy LOL [b] In all seriousness though, I don't really agree with the current "most helpful" negative review. [/b] [list] [*] WIFI: The WIFI disconnecting often is a deliberate gameplay mechanic designed to punish you if you spam the panic button. My WIFI went off every 10 minutes until I figured this out lol. [*] Sound Cues: Having to turn up your volume to listen for audio cues can be a bit annoying, but it's easily solved if you have a physical volume slider or a keyboard shortcut etc. [*] Price: The development team is tiny, so I think the price is pretty fair for what you get. [/list] [h3] Bugs and Dev Support [/h3] I’ve encountered a few bugs, including one game-breaking issue where VirtMesh wouldn't open. However, the developer is incredibly active in the discussion boards. I've even reported another bug myself, the dev replied, and it was patched just a few hours later. Pushing out three or four patches in four days suggests the game probably should have been released in Early Access. But considering how small the team is, bugs are to be expected with an indie launch, and I'm grateful for how fast they are being fixed. [h2] Final Verdict: [/h2] Highly recommended. It has some rough edges, but the atmosphere and dev support make it well worth it. These games are really unique and immersive and you won't really find a similar experience elsewhere unless you count my stupid FNAF comparison that I'm sure will make someone angry lol.

I have played WTTG 1 and 2 as well as scrutinized, and am heavily informed on dead signal. Welcome to the game is my favourite horror series of all time, hands down. But i feel this one is losing the plot. The good: The atmosphere is very creepy, the openness reminds me a lot of FNAF 2. More killers is good, big creepy hillbillies that are addicted to drugs? Awesome! Performance isn't the worst thing ever while looking creepy and pretty at some points. The BAD: Bugs, oh my god the bugs. From several bugs I've been completely soft locked. While these are being fixed slowly you shouldn't release a game as a full product in this state you could've just called this early access and this would've been solved which brings me to my next point; 3/5 of the promised endings are just flat out missing. again just call this early access or delay the game again for Christs sake. The UI is just so weird, typos everywhere. Very bloated especially in the buy menu. The UGLY: RNG VS SKILL. This game is heavily based on RNG to play, hell there is a literal slot machine that can just fully win you the game if you are lucky. Fun but for a rage horror game it doesn't work. Previous games have had RNG as a big factor as well sure, but this one takes the cake. The killers just don't feel like reflect studios killers. If there was a neutral recommendation for this game, I would put it as that. I had fun but a frustrating time with this game. A lot of the mechanics in the game can get really irritating after playing for some time. This was my first WTTG but had played Scrutinized and Dead Signal in the past. The game is fun, to a point. You sit down at your PC, get your software to mount into other PC and browse the dark web when suddenly your power goes out. You go outside to fix the power, you go back inside, sit down to browse for keys again. Then the internet goes out. So you get up again to go outside and fix the internet. You hear a shuffle behind you, you stand still for a few moments until you hear again. Good, I fixed the internet. Time to go back and look for keys and whilst you're in the middle of that, you get hacked. Then as you're in the midst of your hack, maybe even just as you are being hacked, your motion sensor starts going crazy meaning Lucas is coming. It's fine I've turned off the lights to reduce his search time. So you go hide in the laundry basket. Oh b*llocks, I forgot to turn my PC off because of the hack, Lucas stole my DOS coin (Does he bring a USB key with him??) so I'm set back after just getting enough to buy another mine tool or grid upgrade. As you leave the laundry basket, the sudden twang of a banjo calls upon you to go look for the motel room door with the ace of spades on it. Better run out there and into the room until I hear the triumphant fanfare! You sit back down to finally look for some keys after scouring countless website and beating numerous hacks, you forgot something. Drugs. GUESS I'LL GO LOOKING FOR METH. You get your drugs, great, that's one less issue to worry about. You hear a rustling on your left meaning Tanner is lurking and going to bum rush the main door, you hold him off by pressing the panic button (Gonna be honest, did not have much of an issue with Tanner or Lucas because of the way my motion sensors were setup). He's gone, back to looking for keys. After dealing with that over and over again, you finally have about two keys. You gotta scourge the ACRS chat to find someone to drecrypt them for you (and you gotta wait on that) and to find the 2nd and 3rd wikis, all while in the process of still dealing with the power, internet dropping and threats. Meanwhile threats get amped up when you find keys. Oh you forgot to check the other players. Bitstriker and Bikerq4 and getting there pretty fast with their keys and it's only 12:30. Better hire a hacker, doxxer and then a hitman to get rid of them, which means saving your money, hoping you have enough equipment to get you through and of course you have some trusty meth on standby, whilst ALSO hoping you get the RNG that someone can show up in the chat to do those. Scouring for keys on websites can be pretty tiring and it can be pretty easy to gloss over where exactly a key is because you missed a clickable word. That was more frustrating than searching the source code or just the key being right in front of you. It was more of a relief to find keys than it was exciting to find one. If you find one and you die, the key will be on the same website just in a different area and it will still be the same string of numbers and letters (Use steam's notepad or windows' notepad even though some might consider that "cringe"). I did enjoy it to a degree. I like the atmosphere of ReflectStudios games because they feel tense, seedy, ominous etc. The only other game that has an atmosphere that reminds me of it is Ready Or Not. And I am a bigger lover of atmosphere in games, so I enjoyed that. It was fun for a while looking for keys, then it just became tiring. The tension in the beginning was also fun. Not knowing when things would happen or kick off. I'll be honest and say I didn't have much trouble with the threats. Once you figured them out, they were a non issue and anytime they got me, was because I messed up. The threats just become a case of "Would you just f*ck off" after a certain amount of time and were really annoying. Same with the outages. I kind of wish there were more creepy or erieness to the threats. Like maybe you see Tanner peaking out at you from the windows/doors of the motel rooms or he'd be creeping behind the cars in the yard or he was hiding in one, behind the trees etc. Maybe you find Cletus passed out on one of the beds. The breather walking down the road, or maybe you catch a glimpse of him in the woods, stalking the place or like WTTG 2 where the Noir appear in windows. They kind of just become a gimmick or nuisance after a while. So overall would I recommend this game? Kinda? It's frustrating and tedious. I did get annoyed/frustrated with it a lot. I did spend 4 days in a row playing it. It is a time consuming game. If you've played the other games, you know what you're getting into. If not, you better have some patience within you.

I like this game. I like this series. The same problem persists across them all, and the notorious dev is acting the same way he always does about it. The audio mixing is intentionally horrible. You NEED to have the game audio maxed, and you NEED to have your speakers blaring loud to hear ANY audio cue (and you NEED to hear the audio cues, or you have genuinely zero hope of ever beating any of the games). But when you have all these audio settings set to adequate levels for standard gameplay, any time a "jumpscare" happens your entire audio system detonates the building like a nuclear bomb. And there's no way to modulate or adjust that. Thankfully, I'm blessed enough to have a sound system sophisticated enough that I can put a compressor/limiter on my audio output so that the jumpscares have their dynamic range crunched down a bit. But even still, it's not enough. Adam, I have no personal qualm with you. I harbor no ill will against you. You make cool, fun games, and your audio design is very good (the mouse click sounds, keyboard noises, and everything is made so satisfying and sounds awesome). And I like WTTG2 and WTTG3 seems to be even better. But you've gotta get off this horse you're on about requiring people to subject themselves to hearing damage just so they can hear your mandatory audio cues. Please make an accessibility setting to adjust the dynamic range of the sounds in the game. I'm sure you might think that's some form of "easy mode" or that it takes away from your vision of the game, but I value my hearing and I require my ears for my work. And I spend a lot of money on my sound system. I can't have your jumpscare sounds hurting my ears or breaking my equipment. Also, I have to say it, shock scares (i.e., nearly all of the "scares" in this game) are not scary when you're forced to subject yourself to them because you can't play the game without turning your game up loud enough that a nuclear bomb detonates any time you get hacked or die. It genuinely turns me off from playing the games, and I really like the games and want to play them and beat them. It's kind of ridiculous. And you disagree with me, I know. At the minimum, can't you make a "Low/Medium/Loud (default)" setting for the sounds classified as shock content? The dynamic range disparity is genuinely unplayable, I hate to say it. Because I love these games.

I sadly cannot recommend this game in its current state. This game has a lot of potential and I want it to be better. However, you're basically paying to be a game tester. To be fair, the developer is cranking out tons of patches and tweaking the game here and there. Although, you don't get props when the game has this many problems and you sell it as a finished product. It would be a different story if the price was less and it was in early access. The audio cues are way too quiet. You can turn game volume up a lot, but then your ears bleed when you get hacked. When I'm browsing the dark net, sometimes it moves so incredibly slow and it's such a chore to find keys. Loading websites takes a bit of time in the first place, then sometimes there's massive delays when you click something and you have to wait an extra 5-10 seconds. Browsing the internet in the game is just too buggy and slow. There were some problems in the first couple of days of the release where you would almost never see certain enemies, at least I wasn't seeing anyone. There were also some times where death was unavoidable because of a bug. Since then, there have been a decent amount of fixes. I just can't give a pat on the back to the developer for fixing core game mechanics that should have been functional in the first place. Above everything else right now, I really need the dark net to be fixed. I like this game, but it desperately needs work.

idk, I don't know if this games for me but regardless as someone whos pretty new to the series I still feel its fair that I critique it in some form or fashion. Firstly, I couldn't seem to survive past the first hour, and the only time I did, was cause Tanner didn't spawn and immediately instakill me, the enemies aside, its the least of my worries in comparison that to all of the other mechanics that require your attention. Dearest reader, I have a question for you, How are you suppose to: Make DOS, if you have to surf the web and chat with viewers in game, but when you surf the web, your internet goes out in 4 minutes, than while your fixing your internet, your power goes out, so you have to go to the power patch panel and flip the power back on and then fix the internet patch panels, than go all the way back to your desk and sit down only for your internet to go out a 2nd time 40 seconds into your dive on the computer. You get up, to repair it, get ransacked of your meth, but survive. go back to your computer, get hacked, than your internet goes out again. How many inconveniences can you experience before something doesn't feel like its worth even trying for anymore? This game, has a pacing issue, is what I'm getting at, and somehow thats the worst part of this game. There is a lack of balance and delay between inconveniences that knock you over the head, both physically and metaphorically. The wierdest part is that it seemingly only happens to me, cause I'll watch other people play and they seem to get pretty far but everytime I boot the game, I have to fight my internet service provider more than the psychotic killers on the streets. Worse yet, I'd say my 2nd least favorite part of this game is the audio balancing. Shock or Jumpscare horror is cheap, and miserable, I prefer games like Amnesia (the bunker) Darkwood for their atmospheric approaches to horror that build dread instead of hitting you over the head with it. This game could be like the two I just mentioned, but instead, it relys on some of the worst audio balancing I've seen for a video game, to get a cheap scare out of you. Worst yet, Audio ques are key to staying alive but you have to basically subject yourself to the risk of going deaf to hear them. After seeing V4H's review of wttg2 and watching his entire interview with adam, I had nothing but interest in checking out this game. I even wanted to attempt to beat it. I still think deep down that its possible that this game can get into a state where I could beat it. I know bro wants it to be hard. good for him. But its not in a state where i feel like I could beat it.
